decision: Guard-free page-aligned execution closes the dedicated RX 7900 XTX c1 frontier at 129,024 total tokens (126 Ki, 504 pages): one natural request completes exactly at 23.962624 GiB peak with 0.021751 GiB sampled headroom and clean ownership, while the next 256-token page stalls raw startup warmup beyond 600 seconds and 130,048 tokens (127 Ki, 508 pages) returns HIP OOM. On W7900, the same pure-INT8 route passes the model-native 262,144-token c1 limit with 15.543076 GiB headroom. W7900 c2/c4/c8 all pass 8,192 tokens/request but all fail resident_prepare at 8,448 with NotImplementedError; the non-streaming soak's HTTP coalescer submitted c4 as two c2 groups and offered c8 as c1+c3+c4 groups, so those rows do not test live continuous membership. A separate W7900 staggered-SSE gate at 512 prompt + 24 decode tokens qualifies the short mirrored route's resident lifecycle: the first c1 was observed decoding before c4 joined, occupancy moved 0->1->4->3->2->1->0, all four outputs exactly matched their c1 token oracles, admitted/reclaimed deltas were 4/4, and final active/occupied/refcounted ownership was zero. A matched W7900 BF16-vs-INT8 mixed_v1 gate at 129,024 prompt tokens and 16 teacher-forced decode steps passes with mean/max KL 0.000010379/0.000135450, 100% top-1, finite logits, all 16 full-attention layers INT8, and zero BF16 mirror bytes.

raw_artifacts.failure: Configured zero warmups made the generic gate false, and the live helper still sent blocking requests; it proved only queue arrival before the first HTTP response, not controlled-SSE resident admission.

limitations: The XTX 129,024-token row is one natural request with only 0.021751 GiB sampled headroom; it is a measured physical ceiling, not a margin or reliability recommendation.
The 129,280- and 129,536-token startup failures are bounded 600-second warmup stalls, not returned OOMs. The 130,048-token row is the first returned HIP OOM in the narrowed bracket.
The 129,024/16 quality row is the explicit mixed_v1 bounded control. Complete category coverage remains at 512 and 4K; do not call the 129K row a complete long-context suite.
W7900 c2/c4/c8 8K rows retain BF16 mirrors and therefore do not demonstrate compact-INT8 memory savings.

The capacity soak used non-streaming blocking requests and therefore did not test live admission/reclaim. Its /ready continuous_decode=false field was a hardcoded telemetry default, not an engine-capability verdict.

The separate 512/24 controlled-SSE gate qualifies short mirrored-INT8 live admission and reclaim only; cancellation, default elastic pool behavior, overload rejection, and compact no-mirror c>N remain untested.
No throughput or latency claim is made from these capacity, correctness, and lifecycle rows.
next: Qualify cancellation, default elastic pool growth/shrink, and overload rejection on the controlled-SSE route. Then implement and qualify direct no-mirror c>N INT8 attention; the existing short mirrored path is not an INT8 memory-saving route even though its continuous admission/reclaim lifecycle now passes.
